proposals.explanation: The current Ambire extension/mobile onboarding docs list only hardware wallet, seed phrase, and EOA import methods with no passkey/WebAuthn option.
Email+password signup existed only in the deprecated legacy v1 web wallet, and Ambire's docs confirm email+password accounts cannot be created/imported in the current extension.
The extension onboarding requires creating or importing a smart account (via seed phrase/hardware wallet/EOA) with no try-without-wallet or guest/view-only entry point documented.

Ambire creates a smart-contract account, but the current product provisions it from a user-controlled seed phrase or EOA key rather than a no-seed social/email/MPC embedded flow (the legacy no-seed email option is deprecated).
Argent (now Ready) offers an email-based browser web wallet on Starknet that requires no app download or extension, per its support docs.
Argent supports only Ethereum, EVM L2s, and Starknet; there is no evidence of native Sui support in any official source.
Argent supports only Ethereum, EVM L2s, and Starknet; no official source indicates native Aptos support.
Argent supports only Ethereum, EVM L2s, and Starknet; no official source indicates native Cardano support.
Argent supports only Ethereum, EVM L2s, and Starknet; no official source indicates XRP Ledger support.
Argent is a smart-contract wallet that replaces seed phrases entirely, using email/password login and guardian-based social recovery instead.
Argent's web wallet creates a self-custodial smart-contract account behind email/password login with no seed phrase, matching an embedded/smart-account onboarding model.
The Base App's Base Account lets users sign in/create an account using an email one-time passcode (OTP), per Coinbase Help and Base docs on user onboarding.

Base App requires creating a Base Account (smart wallet via email/passkey) on sign-up to access the app, with no documented guest/browse-without-wallet mode, per the Base App launch announcement stating users receive a Base Account upon sign-up.
Bitget Wallet's official blog announced adding the Cosmos (ATOM) mainnet, enabling token transactions and Cosmos ecosystem DApp/DeFi access.
Bitget Wallet's official ADA wiki page instructs users to create a native 'ADA (Cardano) Wallet' from the mainnet list to store, send and receive ADA on the Cardano mainnet.
Bitget's official news announced integrating the XRP Ledger (XRPL) mainnet so users can send/receive XRP and RLUSD and do XRPL cross-chain transactions within the wallet.
Bitget Wallet's keyless MPC integration lets users create a wallet via an email address (along with Google, Apple ID, and Telegram).
Bitget Wallet offers a keyless MPC embedded wallet created via social/email login with no seed phrase, distributing key shares via a 2/3 TSS scheme.
Brave Wallet is built natively into the Brave browser, not offered as a standalone browser-based web app usable without installing Brave.
Brave Wallet natively supports Bitcoin, letting users create Bitcoin accounts and send/receive native BTC across Legacy, SegWit, and Taproot address types.
Brave Wallet's supported networks (Ethereum/EVM, Solana, Filecoin, Bitcoin, Zcash, Cardano) do not include Cosmos SDK/IBC chains.
TON is not among Brave Wallet's supported networks listed by Brave.
Sui is not among Brave Wallet's supported networks.
Aptos is not supported; community reports confirm Brave Wallet cannot be used with Aptos apps/bridges.
Brave and Input|Output completed native Cardano integration, letting users hold and manage ADA and Cardano native assets, send/receive, and swap directly in the wallet.
Brave Wallet does not support the XRP Ledger, as confirmed by community reports that XRP cannot be stored in Brave Wallet.
Brave Wallet onboarding uses a password plus seed-phrase creation/import, with no passkey/WebAuthn signup option.
Onboarding does not require or offer email signup; users only set a password and create/import a seed phrase.
Brave Wallet is a self-custody wallet created via seed phrase, with no no-seed embedded/MPC/smart-account social-login option.
Coinbase Wallet offers a browser-based web app at wallet.coinbase.com with 'no app, extension, or download required' and instant passkey wallet creation.
The Base Account / Smart Wallet is created and accessed via passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID, or a hardware key) instead of a seed phrase, per Coinbase Help.
Coinbase states you can sign in to your Base account using email passcodes, and the smart-wallet onboarding pairs a passkey with an email address.
Base Account is an ERC-4337 smart wallet created behind the scenes via passkey/email login with no seed phrase, matching the embedded/MPC/smart-account model.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs list only EVM chains plus Solana and Tron; Bitcoin is not among the supported networks.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs list only EVM chains plus Solana and Tron, with no Cosmos SDK/IBC support.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs cover only EVM chains, Solana, and Tron; TON is not supported.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs cover only EVM chains, Solana, and Tron; Sui is not supported.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs cover only EVM chains, Solana, and Tron; Aptos is not supported.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs cover only EVM chains, Solana, and Tron; Cardano is not supported.
Daimo's official Supported Chains docs cover only EVM chains, Solana, and Tron; the XRP Ledger is not supported.
Elytro ships as a Chrome browser extension (and a CLI for agents), not a browser-based web app usable without installing anything, per the Chrome Web Store listing and elytro.com.
Elytro explicitly requires no seed phrase, letting users create a wallet with a simple passcode and recover via trusted contacts, per its Chrome Web Store description.
Elytro creates a no-seed ERC-4337 smart contract account behind the scenes accessed via passkey/passcode with social recovery, per its official FAQ and Chrome Web Store listing.
Exodus ships as desktop, mobile, and a browser extension (Exodus Web3 Wallet); there is no browser-based web app usable without installing an app or extension.
Exodus has a dedicated Cosmos ATOM wallet supporting send/receive/stake of native ATOM.
Exodus lists SUI as a supported native asset (Sui and TON went live for send/receive/swap).
Exodus natively supports Aptos (APT) including APT staking via its knowledge base and asset list.
Exodus has a dedicated ADA Cardano wallet supporting native manage/send/stake of ADA since 2020.
Exodus offers a dedicated XRP wallet supporting native XRP on the XRP Ledger.
The consumer Exodus wallet onboards via a 12-word seed phrase; the passkey/MPC 'Passkeys Wallet' is a separate developer/embedded SDK product, not the consumer app's signup flow.
Exodus requires no personal information at signup and creates the wallet from a recovery phrase rather than an email address.
The consumer app requires creating or restoring a seed-phrase wallet before use, with no try/view-only guest mode.
The shipping consumer Exodus wallet is a seed-phrase self-custody wallet; the no-seed MPC 'Passkeys Wallet' is a separate embedded-wallet SDK for developers, not the consumer onboarding UX.
Family supports only Ethereum mainnet and EVM L2s (Optimism, Base, Arbitrum, Polygon, zkSync), with no mention of Sui.
Family is Ethereum/EVM-only per its FAQs and makes no mention of Aptos support.
Family supports only Ethereum mainnet and EVM L2s, with no Cardano support mentioned.
Family is an Ethereum-focused EVM wallet and does not support the XRP Ledger.
Family creates accounts via email/SMS plus passkey/password and generates the seed phrase behind the scenes in memory, never exposing it to the user, so no seed phrase is forced at signup.
Family accounts are created and secured using a passkey (stored in the device's Secure Enclave/TPM), with passkey-only setup on iOS.
Family requires creating an account with email or phone to get started, and even view-only wallet tracking is done from within an account, so there is no account-free guest mode.
Family generates the wallet's seed phrase behind the scenes via email/SMS + passkey login without exposing it, functioning as a no-seed embedded-style self-custodial wallet.
Frame is a desktop-native application (with a companion browser extension for connectivity) and offers no browser-based web app usable without installing software, per docs.frame.sh.
Frame's account setup supports only seed phrases, private keys, keystore files, and hardware signers (Ledger/Trezor/GridPlus), with no passkey/WebAuthn option documented.
Frame provides no email-based signup; accounts are added only via seed phrase, private key, keystore file, or hardware signer.
Frame requires importing/adding a signer to function and documents no guest/try-without-account mode.
Frame is a self-custody signer manager (seed/private key/keystore/hardware) with no embedded/MPC/smart-account or social-login wallet mode.
Gem Wallet's official site and Get Started docs list only iOS and Android native apps with no browser-based web app usable without installing.
Onboarding uses a BIP-39 secret recovery phrase exclusively, with no passkey/WebAuthn option mentioned in the setup docs.
The official site states installation requires 'no email or phone number required,' relying solely on a secret recovery phrase.
Gem Wallet offers a Watch Wallet mode where a user pastes an address to monitor balances and transactions without a seed phrase or creating a key-holding wallet.
Gem Wallet is a self-custodial seed-phrase wallet with no MPC/embedded/social-login smart-account mode; the site emphasizes securely saving your own recovery phrase.
imToken Web (web.token.im) is a non-custodial browser-based web app usable directly in a browser with quick passkey account creation, no native app or extension install required.
imToken's official supported-chains list (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Cosmos, Vaulta, TRON, Polkadot, TON, etc.) does not include Solana.
imToken natively supports the Cosmos ecosystem, listing Cosmos (ATOM) and Osmosis among its supported blockchains.
Sui is not present in imToken's official supported-chains list.
Aptos is not present in imToken's official supported-chains list.
Cardano is not present in imToken's official supported-chains list.
The XRP Ledger is not present in imToken's official supported-chains list.
imToken Web onboarding lets users 'Create account with passkey' using the WebAuthn standard and device secure chip for one-tap login.
imToken Web account creation is passkey-based with an account alias; no email-signup option is documented.
imToken Web is powered by Passkey and Account Abstraction, providing a smart-account wallet created behind the scenes with no private key or mnemonic backup required.

The consumer MetaMask wallet only offers Google/Apple/Telegram social login or SRP for signup; passkeys are used only for biometric unlock of an existing wallet, not for creating/accessing a wallet, per MetaMask support docs (https://support.metamask.io/configure/wallet/social-login/).

MetaMask's consumer wallet creation supports SRP and Google/Apple/Telegram social login only, with no email signup option (email passwordless login exists only in the developer Embedded Wallets SDK, not the shipping consumer wallet), per MetaMask support docs (https://support.metamask.io/start/creating-a-new-wallet/).
MetaMask's new-wallet documentation describes only SRP-based and social-login wallet creation with no guest/try-without-wallet mode.

MetaMask's consumer social login (Google/Apple/Telegram) generates the SRP 'under the hood' and backs it up online via key sharding across nodes so the user never manually handles a seed phrase, per MetaMask's announcement and support docs.
The official Bridge Wallet page offers a 'continue on web / Launch app' option pointing to app.mtpelerin.com, a browser-based self-custodial wallet usable without installing the mobile app.

Mt Pelerin's official supported-network list (Bitcoin, Lightning, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, BNB Chain, Celo, Gnosis, Optimism, Polygon, Rootstock, Sonic, Tempo, Tezos, zkSync) does not include Solana.
Sui is not in Mt Pelerin's official list of supported networks for Bridge Wallet.
Aptos is not in Mt Pelerin's official list of supported networks for Bridge Wallet.
Cardano is not in Mt Pelerin's official list of supported networks for Bridge Wallet.
The XRP Ledger is not in Mt Pelerin's official list of supported networks (which covers Bitcoin, Tezos and EVM chains only).
Bridge Wallet onboarding is built around a self-custodial secret/seed phrase with password and biometric/PIN unlock; official support and product pages describe no passkey/WebAuthn signup.
Wallet creation is seed-phrase based and self-custodial; the email/SMS collected is for KYC identity verification to buy/sell crypto, not for creating or accessing the wallet.
Bridge Wallet is explicitly fully self-custodial where the user holds their own secret phrase, with no no-seed embedded/MPC/smart-account wallet created via social/email login.
NuFi's supported blockchains page lists Bitcoin, Ethereum, Cardano, Solana, Tron, Flow and various EVM/SVM chains but no Cosmos SDK/IBC chains.
NuFi's supported blockchains page does not list TON among its supported networks.
NuFi's supported blockchains page does not list Sui among its supported networks.
NuFi's supported blockchains page does not list Aptos among its supported networks.
NuFi's supported blockchains page does not list the XRP Ledger among its supported networks.

NuFi creates a seedless non-custodial wallet behind the scenes via social login using Web3Auth, splitting the private key into shards stored across a decentralized network (MPC-style embedded wallet).
OKX Wallet has a dedicated Aptos (APT) wallet page and help articles for using the Aptos network to store, send and receive APT across app, web and extension.
OKX Wallet provides a dedicated Cardano (ADA) wallet page to securely store, send and receive ADA on the Cardano network.
OKX Wallet has a dedicated XRP Ledger wallet page to store, send and receive XRP natively.
OKX introduced seed-phrase-free onboarding letting users create/access a wallet by signing in with Email (as well as Google/Apple) across app, extension and web.
OKX offers a guest mode on the home page (desktop or mobile browser) to explore wallet features and view a sample wallet without creating one first.
OKX's social/email login creates a no-seed wallet whose private key is generated and stored in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) behind the scenes, with optional export/mnemonic conversion.
Phantom ships only as a browser extension and mobile app with no standalone browser-based web app usable without installing the extension, per its official setup docs and store listings.
Phantom offers a seedless wallet created with Google/Apple login plus a 4-digit PIN where no secret recovery phrase is shown or handled by the user at signup.
Phantom's seedless onboarding uses Google/Apple OAuth plus a PIN rather than a WebAuthn/FIDO passkey, and no passkey signup option is documented.
Phantom lets users create a wallet via 'Continue with Email' (backed by Google/Apple account) plus a 4-digit PIN, as described in its official email wallet blog and help docs.
PillarX is an EVM-only smart-contract wallet supporting Ethereum, Polygon, Base, BNB, Optimism and Arbitrum, with no mention of Sui in its App Store listing or official materials.
PillarX supports only EVM networks per its App Store listing and official site, with no Aptos support referenced anywhere.
PillarX is a multichain EVM wallet (Ethereum, Polygon, Base, BNB, Optimism, Arbitrum, etc.) and no Cardano support is mentioned in its App Store listing or blog.
PillarX supports only EVM-compatible chains and makes no reference to the XRP Ledger in its App Store listing or official materials.
PillarX's own blog lists passkeys, MFA and session keys as upcoming security features rather than currently shipping, indicating passkey signup is not yet available.
PillarX uses Etherspot account abstraction so users log in with social/email and get a smart account deployed in the background without seed phrases, i.e. an embedded/smart-account wallet.

Rabby is distributed only as a browser extension (Chrome/Firefox/Edge), desktop apps (Windows/Mac), and mobile apps (iOS/Android), with no browser-based web app usable without installing something, per its platform listings.
Rabby onboarding creates a wallet via a password and seed phrase (or import), with no passkey/WebAuthn signup option described in setup guides.
Rabby's setup requires creating or importing a wallet (password + seed phrase) with no guest mode to try the app without a wallet first, though a watch-only address feature exists after setup.
Rainbow ships an iOS/Android app and a browser extension only; the official site and store listings offer no standalone browser web app usable without installing the extension.
No official or secondary source lists native BTC support; Rainbow's chain coverage is EVM plus Solana/Sui/Monad, and reviews explicitly note Bitcoin is not supported.
No source indicates Cosmos SDK/IBC support; Rainbow supports EVM chains plus Solana, Sui, and Monad only.
No source indicates TON support; Rainbow's ecosystems are EVM plus Solana, Sui, and Monad.
No reliable source lists Aptos support; only EVM chains plus Solana, Sui, and Monad are named.
No source indicates Cardano support; Rainbow supports EVM chains plus Solana, Sui, and Monad only.
No source indicates XRP Ledger support; Rainbow's supported ecosystems are EVM plus Solana, Sui, and Monad.
Rainbow onboarding generates an HD seed-phrase wallet secured by a local password; no passkey/WebAuthn signup is documented.
Rainbow creates a self-custodial seed-phrase wallet with no email-based account creation option in any documented onboarding flow.
Rainbow offers a watch/impersonation mode letting users follow and view any public address in read-only mode without creating a wallet first.
Rainbow is a self-custodial seed-phrase HD wallet with no no-seed embedded/MPC/smart-account mode created via social or email login.
Safe is available on EVM chains only and its supported-networks documentation lists no non-EVM chains, so it does not natively support Sui.
Safe is deployed only on EVM-compatible chains supporting the same opcodes as its contracts, which excludes the Move-based Aptos network.
Safe supports EVM chains only, so it does not natively support the non-EVM Cardano network.
Safe supports EVM chains only and lists no XRP Ledger deployment, so it does not natively support the XRP Ledger.
Safe{Wallet} requires connecting a signer wallet (e.g. MetaMask, Ledger) as the first step before you can create or use a Safe, offering no guest/browse mode.

The consumer Safe{Wallet} product does not create a no-seed embedded/social-login wallet behind the scenes; it requires the user to bring an existing external signer wallet to control the Safe smart account.
Trust Wallet ships only as a mobile app (iOS/Android) and a browser extension for Chrome/Brave, with no browser-based web app usable without installing an extension or native app.
Trust Wallet SWIFT automatically creates a passkey (FIDO/WebAuthn, biometric-based) when you create the wallet, using it instead of a password or seed phrase.
Trust Wallet SWIFT is a smart-contract wallet powered by account abstraction with passkey-based creation that eliminates the seed phrase, providing a no-seed embedded/smart-account wallet.
The Uniswap Wallet supports only EVM chains (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, etc.) and cannot hold or send native BTC.
The wallet is EVM-only and provides no Cosmos SDK/IBC chain support per its network documentation and reviews.
The wallet supports only EVM chains and has no TON network support.
The wallet supports only EVM chains and has no Sui support.
The wallet supports only EVM chains and has no Aptos support.
The wallet supports only EVM chains and has no Cardano support.
The wallet supports only EVM chains and has no XRP Ledger support.
The in-app wallet lets you spin up a wallet in a few clicks using FaceID, TouchID, or a passkey.
Users can add login methods including Google, Apple, or email for account access across devices.
The new in-app wallet is a no-seed embedded wallet powered by Privy with distributed key material, created via passkey/social/email login.
Zerion supports only wrapped Bitcoin (WBTC) on EVM/Solana and does not support native BTC mainnet storage/sending per its supported networks documentation.
Zerion natively supports Solana, letting users create/hold/manage Solana assets per its help center and Solana wallet page.
Zerion's supported networks are Ethereum/EVM chains, Solana, and TRON, with no Cosmos SDK/IBC chain support listed.
TON is not among Zerion's supported networks (Ethereum/EVM, Solana, TRON).
Sui is not listed among Zerion's supported networks.
Aptos is not listed among Zerion's supported networks.
Cardano is not listed among Zerion's supported networks.
The XRP Ledger is not listed among Zerion's supported networks.
Zerion's standard wallet creation uses a 12-word seed phrase with passcode/password unlock, not passkey signup (passkeys only appear in its separate Account Abstraction API/Safe tech).
The consumer Zerion app requires creating/importing a seed-phrase wallet and does not offer email signup in its onboarding flow.
Zerion lets users add a watch address to track any public wallet without creating or connecting their own wallet, viewing balances/positions.
The Zerion consumer app creates a self-custody seed-phrase wallet with no embedded/MPC/social-login smart-account mode (such tech is offered only via its developer API, not the consumer app).
Zeus's README lists Supported Platforms as Windows and Linux desktop only, distributed as a downloadable executable, with no browser-based web app.
The README states Zeus is 'seedless' and onboarding only requires a username and password to derive the HD wallet, so no seed phrase is forced at signup (seed import is optional).
The README describes signup as entering a username and password hashed with Argon2Id; there is no passkey/WebAuthn/FIDO option.
The README states that the first time you run Zeus you are prompted to enter a username and password to derive a wallet, with no try-before-wallet guest mode.

Zeus derives a self-custodial HD wallet locally from a username/password via Argon2Id/BIP32 with no telemetry or third-party service, offering no social/email-login MPC or embedded smart-account wallet.
